newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Four injured in Swedish Hell's Angels club blast.
newsitem.headline: Four injured in Swedish Hell's Angels club blast.

text.p: Four people were injured when a powerful blast in the Swedish city of Malmo on Thursday morning partially destroyed a clubhouse used by the Hell's Angels bikers' gang embroiled in a Nordic gang war.
The blast took place in an adjacent property in the early hours, police spokesman Lars Hakansson told Reuters.
Flying glass and debris injured four people, including a baby, in nearby buildings and two were taken to hospital, he said. Twenty families were evacuated from their homes after the blast.

The clubhouse was very badly damaged and at least two walls had collapsed, but four people who were in the building and believed to have some connection with the Hell's Angels were unhurt, the police spokesman said.
He declined to say if the blast was linked to a conflict between the Hell's Angels and the rival Bandidos biker gang that has claimed several lives.
"It's too early to link the two," he said.
Several people have died in drive-by shootings and mortar attacks in various parts of the Nordic region as the Hell's Angels and Bandidos vied for "territory" in Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland.
